q: A steel mill asks our Liaoning magnesia refractory plant for carbon data. What counts?
title: Liaoning magnesia refractory carbon data
short: Count CO2 from calcining magnesite, about 1.09 tonnes per tonne of magnesia from chemistry alone, plus kiln fuel and electricity. Refractories are not CBAM goods, so this is a Scope 3 figure for the buyer. Give it per tonne of brick or mix shipped.
audience: Magnesia and magnesia-carbon refractory makers in Liaoning supplying steel mills

p: Calcining magnesium carbonate releases its carbon. Per tonne of pure MgO, the chemistry gives about 1.09 tonnes of CO2; correct for the ore's actual purity.

ul: Coal, gas or petcoke in shaft and rotary kilns.
Electricity, including electric arc fusing for fused magnesia.

p: Refractories are outside CBAM, so the steel mill uses your figure for its own footprint. Give it per tonne of product with the purity and fuel assumptions stated.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.

sources.label: IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard
